level1.text: A crowbar is used as a lever to pull a nail. The pivot of the bar is $0.050\,\text{m}$ from the nail horizontally, and a hand presses the bar vertically down with a force of $80\,\text{N}$ at a horizontal distance of $0.60\,\text{m}$ from the pivot. The bar is light, so its weight can be ignored. With what force does the bar pull the nail up when the bar is at rest?

A light ruler is supported at its middle. On its left, $0.30\,\text{m}$ from the pivot, hangs a mass whose weight is $0.50\,\text{N}$. How large a vertical downward force is needed on the right, $0.20\,\text{m}$ from the pivot, to keep the ruler horizontal?

The combined weight of a wheelbarrow and its load is $620\,\text{N}$, and the common centre of mass is $0.400\,\text{m}$ horizontally from the axle of the wheel. The handles are $1.20\,\text{m}$ horizontally from the axle. With what vertical force must the person pushing the wheelbarrow lift at the handles to keep the barrow at rest on the wheel and the handles?
A uniform plank of mass $12.0\,\text{kg}$ rests horizontally on two supports. The supports are at the ends of the plank. How large is the support force of each support?

At one end of a light rod of length $0.80\,\text{m}$ there is a mass of $2.0\,\text{kg}$ and at the other end a mass of $6.0\,\text{kg}$. How far from the lighter mass is the common centre of mass of the rod, that is, at which point must the rod be supported to stay horizontal?

level2.text: A uniform plank of length $4.00\,\text{m}$ and mass $25.0\,\text{kg}$ rests horizontally on two supports. The supports are $0.50\,\text{m}$ and $3.00\,\text{m}$ from the left end of the plank. How large is the support force of the left support?

A uniform plank of length $3.0\,\text{m}$ and mass $20\,\text{kg}$ has been laid across a ditch, with both ends resting on the ground. A person of mass $70\,\text{kg}$ stands on the plank $1.0\,\text{m}$ from the left end. How large is the support force at the left end of the plank?

A uniform bookshelf has depth $0.400\,\text{m}$ and height $1.80\,\text{m}$, and its centre of mass is in the middle. The shelf is tilted forwards so that it rests only on its front edge. What is the angle of tilt from the vertical when the shelf is at the limit of toppling, that is, when it would topple by itself if the angle grew any more? Answer in degrees.

A forearm is horizontal, and the hand holds a $5.0\,\text{kg}$ kettlebell $0.32\,\text{m}$ from the elbow joint. The weight of the forearm and hand is $15\,\text{N}$, and its centre of mass is $0.15\,\text{m}$ from the elbow joint. The biceps pulls the forearm vertically up at a distance of $0.040\,\text{m}$ from the elbow joint. How large is the force of the biceps?

level3.text: A painter lays a uniform plank ($4.00\,\text{m}$, $20.0\,\text{kg}$) across two trestles so that the trestles are $0.50\,\text{m}$ and $3.00\,\text{m}$ from the left end of the plank. The mass of the painter is $60.0\,\text{kg}$. How far from the left end of the plank can the painter walk, past the right-hand trestle, before the plank starts to topple?

A shop sign hangs from the end of a horizontal uniform rod. The rod has length $1.20\,\text{m}$ and mass $4.00\,\text{kg}$, and its other end is attached to a wall with a hinge.

The sign, of mass $8.00\,\text{kg}$, hangs from the outer end of the rod. A cable runs from the outer end of the rod to the wall above the hinge so that the angle between the cable and the rod is $30.0^\circ$.

How large is the tension force of the cable?

Two people carry a uniform log of length $5.00\,\text{m}$ and mass $90.0\,\text{kg}$ horizontally. The front carrier holds the front end of the log, and can lift with a force of at most $300\,\text{N}$. How far from the back end of the log must the rear carrier hold the log so that the force of the front carrier is exactly $300\,\text{N}$?
